keyFacts.value: At least 3 months after planned departure from Schengen

uk-eta-entry.title: UK ETA or existing UK immigration permission
uk-eta-entry.summary: Travelers with an ETA-eligible passport normally need an ETA before visiting the UK unless they already hold a visa or another listed exemption.
conditions: Irish citizens and people with valid UK immigration permission are among those who do not need an ETA.
An ETA does not guarantee entry and is linked to the passport used to apply.

keyFacts.label: Visa status
keyFacts.value: No visitor visa with an approved ETA or another exemption

keyFacts.label: ETA validity
keyFacts.value: 2 years or until the passport expires

uk-eta-taiwan-entry.title: UK ETA or existing UK immigration permission
uk-eta-taiwan-entry.summary: Travelers using a qualifying Taiwan passport normally need an ETA before visiting the UK unless they already hold a visa or another listed exemption.
conditions: The Taiwan passport must include the identification number issued by the competent authority.
An ETA does not guarantee entry and is linked to the passport used to apply.

keyFacts.label: Visa status
keyFacts.value: No visitor visa with an approved ETA or another exemption

keyFacts.label: ETA validity
keyFacts.value: 2 years or until the passport expires

us-vwp-entry.title: Approved ESTA or valid U.S. visa
us-vwp-entry.summary: Eligible Visa Waiver Program travelers normally need an approved ESTA before air travel to the United States unless traveling on a valid visa.
conditions: Visa Waiver Program travel is normally limited to tourism or business stays of 90 days or less.
Travel history, dual nationality, passport type and carrier eligibility can make a traveler ineligible for the Visa Waiver Program.
An e-passport is required for Visa Waiver Program travel.

keyFacts.label: Visa status
keyFacts.value: Visa-free under the Visa Waiver Program with an approved ESTA

keyFacts.label: ESTA validity
keyFacts.value: Usually 2 years or until the passport expires

us-vwp-transit.title: Approved ESTA or valid U.S. visa
us-vwp-transit.summary: The United States generally requires transit passengers to hold ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program or an appropriate US visa.
conditions: The United States does not provide a general sterile international transit exemption.
Visa Waiver Program eligibility restrictions still apply to transit.

keyFacts.label: Before travel
keyFacts.value: Approved ESTA or an appropriate U.S. visa

conservative-travel-document.title: Passport or accepted travel document
conservative-travel-document.summary: Confirm which travel document is accepted and its minimum remaining validity. National identity cards can replace passports on some regional journeys.
conditions: Check validity on both the arrival date and planned departure date.
Verify blank-page and document-condition requirements.

conservative-transit-permission.title: Transit permission
conservative-transit-permission.summary: Transit rules depend on nationality, connection length, airport transfer route and whether border control is crossed.
conditions: Airside and landside connections can have different rules.
Airport or terminal changes usually require entry permission.

conservative-entry-permission.title: Visa, eVisa or electronic authorization
conservative-entry-permission.summary: Entry permission depends on nationality, residence, purpose, stay length and documents already held.
conditions: Residence permits and valid visas from other countries can create exemptions.
Visa-free entry can still require an ETA or arrival registration.

DELHI_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.title: Collect and recheck at Delhi
DELHI_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.explanation: International-to-domestic passengers at Delhi must collect checked baggage, clear Customs and use the transfer desk, even when the bag is tagged through.

AUSTRALIA_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.title: Collect for Australian border clearance
AUSTRALIA_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.explanation: International arrivals connecting to an Australian domestic flight must collect checked baggage, clear immigration and customs, then recheck it — including on one ticket.

NEW_ZEALAND_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.title: Collect for Customs and biosecurity
NEW_ZEALAND_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.explanation: On arrival in New Zealand, checked baggage must be collected and cleared before an onward domestic flight.

JAPAN_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.title: Collect at the first airport in Japan
JAPAN_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.explanation: For an international arrival connecting to a Japan domestic flight, collect checked baggage for Customs and check it in again.

CANADA_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.title: Canadian transfer process varies
CANADA_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.explanation: Canadian hubs use airport-, origin- and airline-specific baggage transfer programs. Some passengers clear Customs without collecting bags; others must reclaim them.

GENERIC_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.title: Confirm first-port-of-entry handling
GENERIC_INTERNATIONAL_TO_DOMESTIC.explanation: You are arriving internationally and continuing on a domestic flight. Many countries require baggage to be presented at the first point of entry, but the process is country- and airport-specific.

NOT_CHECKED_THROUGH.title: Bag is not checked through
NOT_CHECKED_THROUGH.explanation: The baggage tag does not cover the onward journey, so collect the bag and check it in again for the next flight.

CHECKED_THROUGH_NO_KNOWN_RECLAIM.title: No known reclaim requirement
CHECKED_THROUGH_NO_KNOWN_RECLAIM.explanation: Your bag is checked through and this connection does not match a supported mandatory Customs reclaim rule.

SEPARATE_TICKETS.title: Separate tickets normally require self-transfer
SEPARATE_TICKETS.explanation: Separate bookings are separate journeys, so baggage is normally collected and checked in again at the connection.

CHECK_BAGGAGE_TAG.title: Check the baggage tag
CHECK_BAGGAGE_TAG.explanation: No supported border rule makes pickup certain here, but transfer depends on whether the airline tags the bag beyond this airport.

US_PRECLEARANCE_NOT_CHECKED_THROUGH.title: Collect because the bag is not checked through
US_PRECLEARANCE_NOT_CHECKED_THROUGH.explanation: U.S. border processing was completed before departure, but the baggage tag does not cover the onward flight.

US_PRECLEARANCE_CHECKED_THROUGH.title: Precleared before the U.S. flight
US_PRECLEARANCE_CHECKED_THROUGH.explanation: This flight departs from a CBP preclearance airport, so eligible passengers arrive like domestic travelers and a through-checked bag normally transfers onward.

US_PRECLEARANCE_CONFIRM_TAG.title: Preclearance removes the usual U.S. reclaim step
US_PRECLEARANCE_CONFIRM_TAG.explanation: CBP processing happens before departure from this airport. Confirm that the baggage tag covers the onward flight.

US_SYD_LAX_SCREENING_PILOT.title: Collect unless your flight uses the CBP screening pilot
US_SYD_LAX_SCREENING_PILOT.explanation: U.S. arrivals normally reclaim checked baggage for CBP. A route-specific remote-screening pilot may transfer eligible bags on the American Airlines Sydney–Los Angeles service.

US_FIRST_ARRIVAL.title: Collect at the first U.S. arrival
US_FIRST_ARRIVAL.explanation: Travelers entering the United States from overseas normally collect checked baggage for CBP and recheck it before any onward flight.
